title: A Serial Two-Stage Framework for Robust Multimodal Fake News Detection via Adaptive Reasoning

problem.claim: Sophisticated multimodal misinformation campaigns use synthetic images and stylistically manipulated text to evade detection systems.

gap.claim: Real-world deployment is constrained by the tradeoff among accuracy, inference efficiency, and robustness.

contributions.claim: DAR-Lite is a serial two-stage framework that decouples representation denoising from contextual reasoning.
The framework uses a variational information bottleneck to distill compact, noise-invariant semantic anchors from raw image-text inputs.

Its adaptive reasoning engine combines retrieval-augmented verification, social credibility propagation, dynamic propagation signals, gated cross-attention, and an auxiliary logical fallacy detection task.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that DAR-Lite consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on multiple large-scale benchmarks, particularly under low false-positive constraints.
The authors report that the serial architecture achieves a favorable balance between detection performance and computational cost.

narrative_sequence.summary: Social media misinformation has intensified alongside generative AI, with increasingly sophisticated multimodal campaigns.
Existing multimodal detection models face a deployment tradeoff among accuracy, inference efficiency, and robustness.
DAR-Lite addresses the tradeoff with serial denoising and contextual reasoning stages, including semantic anchoring and adaptive heterogeneous-context reasoning.
The authors report stronger benchmark performance, especially under low false-positive constraints.
The authors report a favorable performance-cost balance supporting practical large-scale deployment.

source_observation.claim: The framework explicitly separates representation denoising from contextual reasoning in a serial pipeline.

interpretation.claim: Separating noise reduction from higher-level reasoning may help manage competing robustness, accuracy, and efficiency requirements.

application.claim: For multimodal detection systems, consider a staged design in which compact semantic representations are produced before context-intensive verification.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this staging benefits other domains or data distributions.

source_observation.claim: The reported gains are emphasized under low false-positive constraints and alongside computational-cost analysis.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation criteria aligned with deployment constraints can reveal practical tradeoffs beyond aggregate accuracy.

application.claim: When assessing applied detection systems, include false-positive operating points and computational cost alongside performance metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract provides no metric values, benchmark names, or details of the evaluated operating points.

unknowns: No benchmark names, metric values, baselines, or experimental conditions are provided.
No ablation results isolate the effects of the individual framework components.
No implementation, dataset, or reproducibility details are provided.
